decision: checked that pstack works in this session before doing anything else
why: the user said to stop if it did not
evidence: ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json, agent types pstack:poteto-agent and pstack:comment-sicko listed
result: works, env setup script already installs it

decision: added .claude/settings.json with the cursor-plugins marketplace and pstack enabled
why: so a session in any environment gets pstack from the repo itself
result: claude plugin list shows pstack enabled

decision: read the brief by rendering the page in headless chromium
why: a plain fetch returned only an error shell because the brief sits in a sandboxed iframe
result: full brief text saved

decision: chose webhook-as-hint plus refetch over applying webhook payloads to stored records
why: one code path builds state so webhook and reconcile cannot disagree, and duplicate or late events are harmless
result: open until built

decision: verdict is build, but only for re-review inference and the shared whose-turn board
why: github's 2026 dashboard already gives each user a cross-repo inbox, so that part is not a reason to build
result: gap confirmed from docs, not measured in the Atum org

decision: accepted the github boundary from a delegate after rerunning its tests and typecheck myself
why: a delegate's report is not evidence, the rerun is
result: 83 passed, tsc clean, schema check passed 3 queries

decision: split the build into four delegates by directory: core, github boundary, server app, web
why: the directories share only the frozen types in packages/core/src/model.ts and protocol.ts, so they cannot collide
result: core and web and server app in flight, github boundary landed

decision: sweeps compare a cheap fingerprint per pull request and refetch only what changed
why: the delegate estimated a full fetch at about 21 points per 10 pull requests, which would pass the 5000 per hour limit near 300 open pull requests
result: estimate inferred from github's cost formula, not measured

decision: accepted the engine from a delegate, then changed one rule: fully resolved comment threads return the ball to the reviewer
why: the delegate followed my brief to the letter and it left cards in the author's court with zero threads waiting
result: 84 tests pass, tsc clean

decision: wrote scripts/verify-demo.mjs to drive the real server and built client in two browsers
why: unit tests could not show that a change reaches every viewer, so the check had to use the real pages
result: 23 of 23 checks pass, first run caught a missing reason on likely-ready cards

decision: built the image and ran it non-root with a read-only root filesystem
why: the Kubernetes manifest sets those limits, so the image had to be tried under them
result: healthz ok, index served, board returns 12 cards. built with the sandbox proxy CA and a base image mirror added in a scratch copy

decision: ran two adversarial reviewers that had to prove each finding with a run
why: tests written by the builders cannot find what the builders did not think of
evidence: reviewer A report, repro scripts in the session scratchpad
result: reviewer A proved 6 findings, 13 probes held

decision: fixed the stale ready signal in core by giving the signal a timestamp
why: a reviewer who asks for changes again after the author's signal must get the card back to the author
result: 2 new core tests and 1 board test pass

decision: reviewer B proved 11 findings, 3 the same as reviewer A's
why: two reviewers on different models overlap little, which is why the panel has two
evidence: reviewer B report, repro files in its worktree
result: 14 distinct findings in total across both reviewers

decision: kept pending review requests as actors even in an author court
why: the spike says Mine must be at least as good as the GitHub inbox, and the inbox still lists that request
result: core tests pass

decision: added TLS to both ingresses after the reviewer showed sign-in cannot finish over plain HTTP
why: the manifests set https URLs with no certificate
result: manifests parse, not applied to a cluster

decision: fixed all 14 proven findings, each with a test that failed first
why: a finding that a run proved is a bug, not an opinion
result: 397 tests pass, 9 queries pass the schema check

decision: ran the end-to-end check ten times in a row after a delegate reported one unexplained failed run out of eleven
why: a flaky check in CI teaches people to ignore it, so the flake had to be chased before trusting the check
evidence: scripts/verify-demo.mjs, ten run logs in the session scratchpad
result: 10 of 10 runs passed 26 of 26, the earlier failure did not recur and its cause is unknown

decision: replayed the reviewer's oversized webhook against the rebuilt image under the pod's 512 MiB limit
why: the reviewer had killed the container with this request before the fix
result: 413, container still running, not OOM-killed

decision: correction to the row above: 13 of the 14 fixes have a test that failed first, the TLS fix has none
why: the TLS fix changes manifests and the runbook, and nothing here applies them to a cluster
result: 13 fixes tested, 1 untested

decision: replaced the raw manifests in deploy/k8s with one Helm chart
why: two descriptions of the same resources drift apart, so the chart is now the only one
result: 39 chart checks pass, kind could not boot in this sandbox so the cluster install runs only in CI

decision: one workflow gates publishing on tests, chart checks, a kind install, and a two-architecture build
why: a release that skips a gate is the one that breaks, and one file is easier to reason about than three
result: actionlint clean, publish logic dry-run against a local OCI registry, GHCR push itself unproven until the first merge
